verdict: Avoid new steel re-rolling/TMT exposure in Kala Amb; the local demand signal is too weak to offset sector-level margin pressure.
title: Kala Amb steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A Kala Amb re-roller melts scrap or sponge iron in an induction furnace, casts billets, and rolls them into TMT bars sold mostly to local construction and dealer networks. **Cash is made on the spread between scrap cost and TMT realisation, not on volume alone.** The furnace is the single point of failure: a 2026 furnace explosion injured four workers [1] and a 2025 accident at a Kala Amb sariya unit killed one worker [2]. So when a proposal lands, check the furnace age, refractory maintenance log and safety record before anything else; if the unit has had a fatality or explosion in the last 24 months, ask for the factory inspector's closure/restart order and treat it as a hard gate.

**A re-roller's balance sheet is mostly inventory and receivables, so the borrowing base moves with steel prices.** Rating reports on peers flag moderately high working capital needs supported by bank lines [11] and sudden price fluctuations hitting margins [10]. So structure limits against a drawing-power statement on stock and book debts, not a flat term loan; if the customer asks for a clean limit, ask for the last 12 months' stock statements and insist on monthly stock-and-receivable returns.

## What has changed now
Himachal Pradesh GST collections are down 22.8% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], and state electricity demand is down 6.8% against India's +9.5% [D]. **That is a local demand and activity signal, and it is the reason this call is Avoid.** Nationally, IIP for NIC 24 is only +2.4% YoY [D] and Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75-100 band [D], so power and freight costs are against the unit. A steel plant expansion at Kala Amb has already triggered pollution objections [3], which means consent-to-operate risk is live. Note the local sources are 2025-26 and the rating reports are older (2023-24) [8][9][10][11]; treat them as background, not current.

## Where the growth is, and who to avoid
Peer results are strong but they are not Kala Amb: Steel Exchange India reported ~Rs 340 crore Q2 FY27 revenue, up ~45% YoY [6], Rathi Steel over Rs 200 crore, up over 30% [7], and JSW Steel posted 20% EBITDA margin with gearing at 0.42 [5]. **Pursue only integrated or partly integrated units with own billet, branded TMT and a clean safety record; avoid pure conversion job-workers and units dependent on one dealer.** If a proposal is a standalone re-roller with no captive billet and no brand, decline; if it is a branded TMT unit with a national or regional brand premium [9], consider a small working-capital line with a stock audit.

## How to grow safely and what to watch
Take monthly stock statements, quarterly GST returns, electricity bills and furnace production logs. **Covenant the account on drawing power and on safety compliance, not just turnover.** Collect from customer the current order book, dealer-wise receivables ageing and power tariff, since the data pack has no Kala Amb-specific figures.

- Monthly: electricity bill vs prior year -> a fall beyond the state's -6.8% [D] means the furnace is idling; ask why. - Event: any furnace accident or pollution notice [1][2][3] -> stop disbursement and inspect.
